reason: The cited evidence (E1) only states that adding Mo increases room-temperature strength and adding Nb increases ductility in a different alloy system (Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr). It does not address electronegativity differences, stress concentrations, or the specific NbZrTiHfMo system, leaving most key premises unsupported.
premises: High Mo content increases electronegativity difference and reduces plasticity in NbZrTiHfMo.
Reducing Mo by substituting with Nb lowers electronegativity mismatch.
Lower electronegativity mismatch enhances ductility by reducing stress concentrations.
Solid solution strengthening is maintained after partial Mo replacement by Nb.
The disordered BCC phase is preserved upon Nb substitution.
